chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not create for people absolute freedom in their actions, but He gave them choice and free will. So whoever chooses good, Allah chooses it for him, and whoever chooses evil, Allah chooses it for him.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on free will and divine choice?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq articulates the Shia doctrine of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (the matter between the two matters), rejecting both absolute determinism (*Jabariyya*) and total human autonomy (*Tafwid*). This hadith emphasizes that while Allah creates the capacity for choice, He affirms the individual's free will (*ikhtiyar*) in executing their actions, thereby ensuring divine justice in reward and punishment.
